Scale · choosing the steps

Where a scale starts and ends, and how far apart its steps are, instead of the fixed 50 … 950. Home, the bar, the field and the preview come from the app’s own code at 80 × 24. The ramp is redrawn so it fits any number of steps. Switch dark and light at the right of the tab bar.

The line under the ramp now starts with which set of steps, the way online generators do it. Tailwind is the 50 … 950 you have today, and you can still trim its ends. Even takes a count instead of “every”: 3 to 21 steps spread evenly from one end to the other, named by where they fall, to the nearest 10. Your colour is always one of them: the count is split between the lighter side and the darker side, in proportion, so 500 is always a step. Radix is their twelve, numbered 1 – 12, with your colour at 9 where Radix puts its solid colour, light backgrounds and borders above it and text colours below. The first value in the line is now the set: ←→ changes it, and tab goes on to what that set lets you change.

V1 with your two changes. r make centre steps back into the quiet keys at the right, beside # new colour. Pressing s turns the line’s s steps into ↵ done in the same place, so the key that finishes sits where you started. The key row while editing keeps only ←→ change and tab next, with esc cancel at the right. Home: Scale reads create shades from one colour.

Three ways to change where the scale starts, where it ends and how far apart its steps are. Each figure is a few moments, left to right: the scale as it is, changing the start, changing the spacing, and the result. The ramp redraws as you change a value, so you see the steps before you commit. The Steps tab explains the rules all three share.

The numbers are places on a ruler from 0 (near white) to 1000 (near black), with your colour always at 500. Start and end choose how much of the ruler you get, and every chooses how many steps: the start, the end, and every multiple of “every” between them. So today’s set is 50 – 950 every 100, which gives 50, 100, 200 … 900, 950. Today’s eleven colours keep their exact hex: a new step like 150 sits halfway between 100 and 200 on the same curve. The script checks this against scale() for five colours.

Limits, and why. Start goes from 0 to 450 and end from 550 to 1000, in 50s, so your colour is always in its own scale. “Every” is 50, 100 or 250. I left out 25 because 0 – 1000 every 25 would be 41 swatches, two cells wide and impossible to tell apart. At most it’s 21 steps (0 – 1000 every 50), and those still fit in 80 columns.

Palette now reads extract colours from an image, as you asked, and here are four lines for Scale.
